# What is blood made of?

<!-- STEP id="parts" -->
## Two main parts
Blood has two main parts. **Plasma** is the liquid part, and it makes up about 55 per cent of the volume of blood. The **formed elements** make up the other 45 per cent: red blood cells (RBCs), white blood cells (WBCs) and platelets.

<!-- STEP id="cut" -->
## A small cut
When you get a small cut on your skin, red blood oozes out, and after some time a clot forms. The red colour comes from **haemoglobin**, an iron-rich protein in the red blood cells. RBCs live for about 4 months and are replaced regularly. **Platelets** help the blood to clot where the skin is injured.

<!-- STEP id="infection" -->
## A skin infection
When the skin is infected, the area turns red and may swell a little, and you may get a fever. White blood cells collect at the infected area. This causes redness and swelling, and sometimes pus forms there.

<!-- STEP id="run" -->
## A run
When you exercise or run, you breathe faster and your face may turn red. Your muscles need more oxygen, so breathing becomes faster and more blood flows through the body.

<!-- STEP id="sum" -->
## Every part has a job

| Experience | What you notice | Part of blood at work |
|---|---|---|
| A small cut | blood oozes, then a clot forms | platelets; RBCs give the red colour |
| A skin infection | redness, swelling, perhaps pus | white blood cells |
| Running | faster breathing, red face | blood carrying more oxygen to muscles |

**Blood is a liquid connective tissue. Next come the firm connective tissues, such as bone and cartilage.**
